thread:
alex: Hey team — Customer C-581 hitting repeated 401s, says there is no request/trace id in the response. Can we confirm what to ask them for so we can escalate?

maya: Ask them for the raw response headers and a minimal curl that reproduces it. Also ask where they’re calling from (browser, server, mobile).

jess: Quick checklist I send customers: 1) a curl that reproduces (include Authorization header obfuscated), 2) the SDK client version, 3) the full response headers, 4) a HAR if browser, or proxy logs if mobile.

alex: They said "server -> our proxy -> Redwood". They attached a snippet but it doesn't include headers.

maya: In that flow we need either the Redwood request id or the proxy correlation id. In our HTTP logs the header we look for is `x-rw-request-id` (or `x-request-id` forwarded by proxies). If they can provide any of those values we can find the trace.

raj: If they can’t find it, ask them to run this quick curl repro (replace key and host as needed):

jess: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hi"}' \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

jess: The important bits are the verbose `-v` output (it prints response headers) and any `x-rw-request-id` in the response. If you get a 401, copy the full headers block and paste it here (mask the token).

maya: For browser HAR: Chrome DevTools -> Network tab -> reproduce -> right click -> "Save all as HAR with content". Send the HAR (or upload to a shared bucket) and point to the request. We can extract our request id or see if the proxy stripped it.

alex: They sent a small server log extract with only bodies. I asked for headers. They replied they don’t see `x-rw-request-id` in their logs.

raj: If proxy strips headers, ask them to add a temporary passthrough rule to forward `x-rw-request-id` or to log `response.headers` from their HTTP client. Also ask for the request timing window — e.g., "approx time 2026-03-16T14:02:30Z" — helps narrow server logs.

jess: We also support a debug token flow for private consoles: in Console -> Requests -> search by path -> open the request -> Copy debug token (button). That token contains the internal trace pointer. If they can paste it here we can pull the full trace without sharing other customer data.

alex: Good point — customer is on Dedicated, they have Console access. I'll ask them to try the debug token and to attach a HAR from the proxy side.

support-bot: NOTE: Please redact any PII and API keys before uploading. Use secure upload (S3 pre-signed or our support collection link).

maya: Also request the SDK version string (e.g., `@redwood/sdk-js@1.3.2`) — some older SDKs had different header names.

jess: Example JS snippet they can run to log the response header if using fetch:```
fetch(url, opts).then(r => { console.log('status', r.status); console.log('headers'); console.log([...r.headers.entries()]); });
```

alex: Great. I'll message customer with: minimal curl (-v), full response headers (mask token), proxy HAR or proxy logs, approximate UTC time, SDK version, and Console debug token if available.

raj: If they can't get any request id, we can still search our ingress logs for their IP + timestamp window, but that takes longer. Tell them that up front.

alex: Sent the request to the customer, asked for upload to our support bucket. Marking for follow-up — ping me if they post anything here. :thumbsup:
